articles.title: India-Pakistan handshake row: MCC admits it cannot force players to shake hands - India Today
articles.summary: India-Pakistan handshake row: MCC admits it cannot force players to shake hands India Today
articles.content: The India-Pakistan handshake row has once again come into focus after the two teams avoided the customary exchange of greetings following their Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha on Sunday. While the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) is the custodian of the Laws of Cricket, it has little authority over such decisions, with matters involving player conduct and international cricket falling under the jurisdiction of the International Cricket Council (ICC) and, in certain cases, individual cricket boards.India A, led by Tilak Varma, lost to Pakistan on Sunday, but the absence of handshakes once again drew attention. Players from the two sides did not exchange greetings either before or after the match, continuing a practice followed by Indian cricket teams since last year's Asia Cup in Dubai.The MCC and the ICC have distinct roles in the administration of cricket. The MCC, founded in 1787, is responsible for maintaining, interpreting, and updating the Laws of Cricket, which define how the game is played. The ICC, meanwhile, is the global governing body of international cricket. It oversees international tournaments, frames playing conditions and enforces its Code of Conduct, which deals with player behaviour and disciplinary matters.While the MCC can advocate sportsmanship and fair play, it cannot compel players to shake hands or intervene in decisions taken by teams and their governing boards."If there are edicts coming from above about handshakes, that's not something that MCC can control. We would like to see it, but we realise there are bigger issues at play, and that's something beyond our control," Fraser Stewart, the MCC's Laws Manager and Head of Cricket, said.India A vs Pakistan A, Rising Stars Asia Cup HighlightsStewart, who is in the UAE for the ongoing ILT20 season, declined to comment directly on the no-handshake policy followed during India-Pakistan matches, saying the issue went beyond cricket."There are certain instances that transcend cricket and come from a level that's above my station to talk about geopolitical situations. What we can control is that, on the field, the players respect each other, they respect the umpires, the authority of the umpires and the game," he said.He added that the MCC could only focus on conduct within the sport and had no authority to challenge decisions taken at a higher level.FREE HITS IN TEST CRICKET? MCC OPEN TO IDEAStewart also revealed that the MCC could consider introducing free hits after no-balls in Test cricket.Free hits are currently part of the playing regulations in limited-overs cricket but are not included in the Laws of Cricket. The MCC has discussed extending the provision to all formats but has not taken a decision."Free hits, they're not in the laws at the moment. It's something we will consider. So they only exist as playing regulations," Stewart said."We've discussed it, but at the moment we've stopped short of bringing free hits into all cricket, but you never know. Eventually we'll get there," he added.MCC LOOKS TO MAKE CRICKET LAWS MORE ACCESSIBLEThe MCC is also working with national sports bodies to translate cricket's laws into regional languages, making them easier for players and fans to understand.The rule book is now available in Hindi, Urdu, Kannada, Marathi and Bangla, alongside English. Stewart said he had visited India in October to launch the translations and was headed to Sri Lanka to introduce two more language versions."I was in India at the beginning of October launching that, and we have it in Urdu, Hindi, Kannada, Marathi and Bangla, as well as English, obviously. And I'm off to Sri Lanka tonight, and we'll be launching it in two more languages for Sri Lankan people," he said."Part of our role is to make the game accessible. The laws are complicated. They're not an easy read, particularly when they're not in your first language, so it's on us to try to make those laws understandable," Stewart added.- EndsMust Watch

articles.title: Tilak Varma blames lack of partnerships for India A's Asia Cup loss to Pakistan - India Today
articles.summary: Tilak Varma blames lack of partnerships for India A's Asia Cup loss to Pakistan India Today
articles.content: India A captain Tilak Varma rued the lack of partnerships in the middle order after his team suffered a 48-run defeat to Pakistan A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament on Sunday.Chasing 314, India A were in deep trouble at 129 for six before Tilak and Shahbaz Ahmed put together a 112-run stand for the seventh wicket. Shahbaz scored 56 off 41 balls, while Tilak remained unbeaten on 100 off 149 deliveries. However, their efforts were not enough as India were bowled out for 265.Tilak felt Shahbaz's dismissal came at the wrong time, just when the two were looking to step up the scoring. He believed another couple of overs from the all-rounder could have changed the course of the chase."The way Abhishek started and the way Shahbaz gave me a partnership in between was crucial. Unfortunately, when we wanted to accelerate, Shahbaz got out. Otherwise, if he could have stayed for another two overs, I could have finished the game," Tilak said after the match.India A vs Pakistan A, Rising Stars Asia Cup HighlightsAbhishek Sharma had given India a flying start with a 42-ball 70, but his dismissal left the middle order with plenty to do. The Indian batters struggled to maintain the scoring rate, with Pakistan's bowlers picking up wickets at regular intervals.Tilak also credited Pakistan's fast bowlers for their disciplined effort but felt India let the game slip by losing wickets in quick succession."The second half was slightly swinging initially, in the first 10 overs. Credit goes to those two fast bowlers who bowled very good lines and lengths. But at the same time, we lost back-to-back wickets in between. Otherwise, we could have sealed the game in the 47th or 48th over," he said.Despite scoring a century, Tilak was not keen to call it one of his best batting performances. For the India A captain, the result mattered more than his individual effort."I won't say that. For me, the best is winning the game. If I don't win the game, then it's not the best for me. But I always want to take it as deep as possible. Today, I was looking for that. If any other batter could have given me support, then I could have finished the game," he said.Tilak also spoke about the responsibility that comes with leading the side, saying he enjoys taking the team through difficult situations."If you are a captain for the team, then you should take that load and responsibility. So, yeah, I honestly love doing that. At the end of the day, God is kind and he has given those runs to me," he added.Earlier, Hasan Nawaz top-scored for Pakistan A with 79, while Maaz Sadaqat (59) and Farhan Yousaf (56) made valuable half-centuries to take their side to 313 all out. Pakistan's bowlers then finished the job, handing India A a 48-run defeat despite Tilak's hundred.- EndsMust Watch

articles.contentMarathi: India A captain Tilak Varma rued the lack of partnerships in the middle order after his team suffered a 48-run defeat to Pakistan A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament on Sunday.Chasing 314, India A were in deep trouble at 129 for six before Tilak and Shahbaz Ahmed put together a 112-run stand for the seventh wicket. articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 21: Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata set for 11th edition on December 20 Sportstar
articles.content: CHENNAI ATHLETICS Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata returns on December 20 The Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata will return for its 11th edition on December 20, with organisers expecting another strong turnout as the event continues to promote fitness, inclusivity and community participation. Promoted by Procam International, the event will be flagged off from the iconic Red Road. With 30 days to go, the organisers said registrations for the 25K category closed in just 14 hours following an overwhelming response. The Open 10K, Champions with Disability, Senior Citizen Run and Ananda Run categories have also received an encouraging response, underlining the event’s growing appeal across age groups and abilities. The event has also received the support of the West Bengal government, with Ashok Dinda, Minister of State for MSME and Food Supply, and Dr. Subrata Gupta, Chief Advisor to the Chief Minister, highlighting its role in promoting physical fitness and sporting participation. “Running a marathon is not as easy as it sounds. It requires dedication, discipline and proper preparation. Having participated in distance runs in Asansol, Tamluk and Kolkata, I understand the physical challenges that come with long-distance running,” Dinda said in a release. “My aim is to prepare well and complete the run on December 20. I hope this edition becomes a historic event where people across Bengal come together, participate and run with the spirit of never looking back.” A major attraction of this year’s edition will be the unveiling of the ‘Medal of Steel’ for 25K finishers. Crafted from Tata Steel, the medal celebrates the endurance, determination and perseverance required to complete the challenging distance. The organisers also unveiled medals for participants in the Open 10K, Ananda Run, Senior Citizen Run and Champions with Disability categories. -Press Trust of India HOCKEY Punjab Hockey League Season 3: Roundglass Hockey Academy score 10 past SDAT Roundglass Hockey Academy registered its second straight win as it thrashed Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) 10-0 in the third edition of Punjab Hockey League at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali on Saturday. Odisha Naval Tata Hockey High-Performance Centre (HPC), meanwhile, kicked off its campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Government Hockey Academy, Sonipat. Naval Tata Hockey Academy, Jamshedpur, came from behind to edge past Namdhari XI 2-1 for its second consecutive win of the league. - Team Sportstar SAILING Indian Navy, Army sailors dominate Senior National Sailing Championships Indian Navy and Army sailors dominated the Yachting Association of India (YAI) Senior National Sailing Championships, with 121 sailors competing in the five-day regatta. A total of 94 boats representing 17 clubs competed across nine Olympic classes, making it the largest Senior National Championships in terms of participation in the last five years. As many as 91 races were completed during the competition held off the Sunk Rock and Prongs Lighthouses. Two-time Olympian and Asian Games bronze medallist Vishnu Saravanan clinched his seventh national title in the ILCA 7 class, winning seven of the nine races. Asian Games 2026 silver medallists Prince Noble and Manu Francis won the 49er title, while bronze medallist Harshita Tomar, partnering Ritika Dangi, topped the 49erFX class after winning nine of their 10 races. Doiphode SI and Ramya Saravanan dominated the Nacra 17 class, winning all 10 races, while Shraddha Verma and Ravindra Kumar Sharma secured their fifth national title in the 470 mixed class. Neha Thakur won the ILCA 6 title, while Aditya Sangwan topped the iQFOiL men’s category. Prarthana Bhoi won the iQFOiL women’s title, and Asish S Roy emerged victorious in Formula Kite men. The championships were conducted by the Indian Naval Watermanship Training Centre, Mumbai, under the aegis of YAI and the Indian Naval Sailing Association. -PTI SNOOKER Anupama defeats Man Yan, retains World snooker title India’s Anupama Ramachandran found her rhythm at the right juncture to outplay So Man Yan and retain her IBSF World Snooker title in Indore on Saturday. After losing the scrappy first frame, Anupama raised her game to score a comfortable 3-1 win over her Hong Kong China rival, becoming the first Indian to win back-to-back crowns. Reacting to the win, Anupama told Sportstar: “I didn’t start very well in the final and I was a little nervous, but I did better. I think I played much better in the last three frames. I am genuinely happy with how I performed throughout the tournament.” Defending the title and winning it in India made the victory special, said Anupama. “I beat Tessa (Davidson) of England 3-1 in the semifinals and Keerthana (Pandian) 3-1 in the quarterfinals. They all pushed me to do my best,” she added. In the men’s title clash, Ali Gharahgozlou of Iran outclassed Hong Kong China’s Tam Yun Fung 5-1. After edging out India’s Pankaj Advani 5-3 in the semifinals earlier in the day, the Iranian enthralled the crowd with a brilliant exhibition of potting and amazing consistency, taking home a USD 10,000 cheque. Anupama, who was richer by USD 4,000 for her splendid triumph, started a trifle tentatively. However, she gathered her wits quickly to put her rival in trouble, making fine runs of 31, 19 and 16 to clinch the second frame. Further breaks of 16, 28 and 18 helped Anupama take a 2-1 lead. In the fourth frame, Man Yan began aggressively with an early 20, but Anupama was equal to the task, making breaks of 14 and 26 before missing the blue to the top-right pocket. But Anupama soon potted a long blue to the bottom-right and the pink to the top-right to retain her title. - PTI GYMNASTICS Maiden Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championship to be held in Mumbai The Indian Navy Sports Control Board (INSCB), on behalf of the Services Sports Control Board (SSCB) and under the aegis of the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI), will host the first-ever Youth Artistic Gymnastics (Men & Women) National Championship 2026–27 at INS Hamla, Malad (West), Mumbai, from November 24 to December 1. The event will bring together approximately 800-plus participants from all States and Union Territories. The men’s national trial will be conducted on November 27, while the women will have it on December 1. -Team Sportstar BASKETBALL ACG Jr. NBA 3v3 Tournament: Millennium National School - Team A, St. Anthony Girls’ High School - Team A crowned winners of Mumbai leg The ACG Jr. NBA 3v3 National Tournament, a nationwide school-based tournament for U-16 boys’ and girls’ teams, concluded its Mumbai leg at Fatima High School, Vidyavihar, Mumbai. The top two boys’ and girls’ teams in each zone and one all-star team from both the boys’ and girls’ divisions in each zone will advance to the ACG Jr. NBA 3v3 National Finals Tournament, to be held in December. Sharanya Sawant from St. Anthony Girls High School and Amey Darwatkar from Millennium National School were recognised with the Skechers MVP Award for their outstanding performance throughout the Mumbai leg of the tournament. Guided by the program’s central theme, “Where Stars Are Born,” the 2026 edition features a shift to an under-16 age classification to engage aspiring players at a more advanced stage of their development. The tournament is being conducted by the National Basketball Association (NBA) in association with ACG, the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), with Skechers as the Official Kit Partner. The tournament is visiting 10 cities across India: Ahmedabad, Indore, Kochi, Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Prayagraj, and Ludhiana. Winners of the ACG Jr. NBA 3v3 Tournament - Mumbai U16 Boys Winners - Millennium National School - Team A (Samar Bhujbal, Vedant Sant, Amey Darwatkar, Soham Godbole) Runner-Up - The Bishops Co-Ed School Undri Pune - Team A (Aaradhya Bhavsar, Aayush Limakr, Ethan Gardner, Rajyavardhan Shekhawat) 2nd Runner-Up - Cathedral And John Connon School - Team A (Samar Hingorani, Anshuman Hooda, Shlok Jain, Anay Arlekar) All-Star Team Mumbai - Aiden Liu (The Bishops Co-Ed School Undri, Pune), Arnav Sawant (Christ Academy, Koparkhairne), Zeon Velekalihill (St. Joseph’s High School Wadala), Sharvil Hublikar (Pawar Public School, Nanded City) U16 Girls Winners - St. Anthony Girls High School – Team A (Chaitra Prabhu, Sharanya Sawant, Vanya Shetty, Avani Kadam) Runner-Up - The Bishops Co-Ed School Undri Pune - Team A (Tanirika Chakraborty, Girija Adnaik, Avni Tambe, Dhruvi Pisal) 2nd Runner-Up - Hutchings High School And Jr College Pune – Team A (Sakshi Vyas, Pranjal Taware, Mrunmayi Bhujbal, Kriya Kaushik) All-Star Team Mumbai - Aditi Tandon (St Mary’s School), Maitri Shah (Indira National School), Anika Nayak (Sardar Dastur Nosherwan Girls High School), Kriya Kaushik (Hutchings High School & Jr College) -Team Sportstar SQUASH Abhay Singh vs Veer Chotrani in men’s final of National squash Former champion Abhay Singh will meet Veer Chotrani in the men’s final of the National Squash Championships at the Otters Club in Mumbai on Sunday. In the semifinals on Saturday, top seed Singh defeated 3/4 seed Rahul Baitha 11-2, 11-3, 11-7, while second seed Chotrani beat qualifier Yash Fadte 13-11, 11-1, 3-11, 13-11. In women’s last-four, 5/8 seed Shameena Riaz edged out top seed Rathika Seelan 8-11, 11-7, 11-8, 8-11, 11-3. Shameena will meet the winner of the second semifinal between Akansksha Salunkhe and Aadya Budhia for the title. Other results — ProCoach (semifinals): 5/8-Atul Kumar Yadav bt 9/16-Anurag 12-10, 10-12, 11-9, 9-11, 13-11; Abhishek bt 1-Matthew Godwin 11-9, 4-11, 5-11, 11-6, 11-6. - Team Sportstar SHOOTING Danish Khan wins Men Skeet Gold at 69th National Shooting C’ship Uttar Pradesh’s Danish Khan won the Master Men Individual Skeet gold medal at the 69th National Shooting Championship Competitions (NSCC) at the Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Ranges on Saturday. The shotgun competitions, organised by the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) under International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) rules, have been underway since 12 November. Danish, who qualified second with 109 (20, 22, 23, 22, 22), shot 29 in the eight-man final to finish two targets clear of the field. Telangana’s J. Jayeshchand, who entered the final in sixth place with 103 (21, 20, 22, 21, 19), took silver with 27. articles.title: Maharashtra withdraws its plea before Bombay High Court against FSSAI - Bar and Bench
articles.summary: Maharashtra withdraws its plea before Bombay High Court against FSSAI Bar and Bench
articles.content: The Maharashtra government has withdrawn its petition before the Bombay High Court against the Union Health Ministry and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over the validity of the central food safety regulations [State of Maharashtra v. Union of India & Ors.]..The plea by the State had claimed that the regulations establishing a parallel enforcement regime and was against the Constitution..The plea was listed before a division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh C Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna on November 21. .When the matter came up for hearing, Advocate General Milind Sathe informed the court that the state wished to withdraw it. As per reports, the withdrawal followed outreach from FSSAI for an out-of-court resolution. Government pleader Neha Bhide informed the court that on instructions from FDA, the petition was being withdrawn. The bench recorded the statement and allowed the withdrawal..The state Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approached the court in September alleging that the Centre and FSSAI had dismantled the decentralised framework of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Under the Act, licensing and enforcement powers belong to State commissioners and designated officers.The petition challenged the 2011 Licensing Regulations, 2018 Recruitment Regulations and 2026 Amendment Regulations. It argued that the FSSAI CEO unlawfully created posts such as ‘Central Food Safety Officer’ and ‘Central Licensing Authority’. According to the plea, the CEO’s enforcement mandate is restricted to imported food articles, not domestic ground operations..The State also contested a May 12, 2023 FSSAI directive barring State officers from inspecting centrally licensed businesses. It claimed the online FoSCoS portal was deployed to systematically bring food businesses under central jurisdiction. The plea further challenged March 10 and March 13 notifications that revised licensing turnover thresholds without inviting prior public objections, citing a violation of Section 23 of the General Clauses Act. In its prayer, the State sought to quash the regulations, stay the 2023 directive and reclaim licensing databases for state officers.

articles.title: PlayForward launches Australia–India sports initiative, signs MoU with NSW Rugby League - Sportstar
articles.summary: PlayForward launches Australia–India sports initiative, signs MoU with NSW Rugby League Sportstar
articles.content: SYDNEY PlayForward, a new Australia–India sporting initiative, was launched at the Parliament of New South Wales on Saturday, alongside the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with NSW Rugby League, as it seeks to strengthen connections between the sporting industries of both countries. The initiative aims to bring sporting organisations, athletes, coaches, clubs, academies, educational institutions and businesses into a shared ecosystem to explore collaboration across multiple disciplines. The launch at NSW Parliament House brought together representatives from Hockey NSW, Surf Life Saving, Squash NSW, Volleyball NSW, Kho Kho Australia, the Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs, Northern NSW Football, UNSW and the Centre for Australia–India Relations, besides the NSW Rugby League. Former Australian Under-19 cricketer Baxter Holt hosted the event. The MoU with NSW Rugby League provides a foundation to explore cooperation in community participation, junior development, coaching, competition structures and player pathways. Specific programmes and deliverables will depend on further discussions between the organisations. READ: Josh Hazlewood backs Pat Cummins in Sandpaper-gate, insists ‘bowlers were not involved’ https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/josh-hazlewood-backs-pat-cummins-sandpaper-gate-bowlers-not-involved/article71727092.ece The partnership comes as the rugby league develops its presence in India. Rugby League India was approved as an Observer Member of International Rugby League in September 2026, while the Indian Heritage Rugby League NSW made its debut at the NSWRL Harmony Nines in October. PlayForward’s broader ambitions align with the India–Australia Roadmap for Sports Collaboration, launched by Prime Ministers Anthony Albanese and Narendra Modi at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on July 10. The roadmap identifies opportunities in high-performance sport, sports science, technology, grassroots participation, women’s sport, para-sport and industry investment. With Ahmedabad preparing to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and Brisbane staging the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, the initiative sees opportunities for collaboration in athlete development, sports education, research, event management and commercial partnerships. Beyond cricket, PlayForward aims to connect organisations across hockey, football, rugby, volleyball, basketball, squash, athletics, kabaddi, Kho Kho and para-sport.
